questions.question: He said, "I am busy now." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said that he was busy then.
options.B: He said that he is busy now.
options.C: He said he was busy now.
options.D: He said that he had been busy then.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech with a past reporting verb ('said'), the present simple tense ('am') shifts to past simple ('was'), and the time adverb 'now' shifts to 'then'.

questions.question: She said, "I finished my work yesterday." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She said she finished her work the previous day.
options.B: She said she has finished her work yesterday.
options.C: She said that she had finished her work the previous day.
options.D: She said she finishes her work the previous day.

questions.explanation: Past simple tense ('finished') shifts to past perfect tense ('had finished'), and the time adverb 'yesterday' shifts to 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

questions.question: He said, "I will go tomorrow." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said he would go the next day.
options.B: He said he will go tomorrow.
options.C: He said he would go tomorrow.
options.D: He said he goes the next day.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'will' shifts to 'would' in indirect reporting, and the time expression 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.

questions.question: She said, "I have been reading this book." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She said she has been reading that book.
options.B: She said that she had been reading that book.
options.C: She said she was reading that book.
options.D: She said she read that book.

questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous tense ('have been reading') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been reading'), and the demonstrative pronoun 'this' shifts to 'that'.

questions.question: The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
options.B: The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
options.C: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
options.D: The teacher told that the sun is rising in the east.

questions.explanation: Universal truths, scientific facts, and habitual actions do not undergo tense backshift even when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

questions.question: She said to me, "Where are you going?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She asked me where was I going.
options.B: She asked me where I was going.
options.C: She asked me where am I going.
options.D: She told me where I was going.

questions.explanation: In indirect interrogative sentences beginning with Wh-words, the reporting verb changes to 'asked', the Wh-word acts as conjunction, and the sentence order becomes assertive (subject before auxiliary: 'I was going').

questions.question: He said to her, "Do you like coffee?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He asked her that did she like coffee.
options.B: He asked her if she liked coffee.
options.C: He told her whether she likes coffee.
options.D: He asked her whether did she like coffee.

questions.explanation: For Yes/No interrogative sentences, the reporting clause connects with 'if' or 'whether', the auxiliary 'do' is removed, and the verb shifts to past simple ('liked').

questions.question: The doctor said to the patient, "Take your medicine regularly." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The doctor advised the patient to take his medicine regularly.
options.B: The doctor said the patient that he should take his medicine regularly.
options.C: The doctor ordered the patient take his medicine regularly.
options.D: The doctor asked the patient taking medicine regularly.

questions.explanation: In imperative sentences expressing medical counsel, the reporting verb becomes 'advised', and the imperative verb is converted into a to-infinitive clause ('to take').

questions.question: The father said to his son, "Do not waste your time." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The father forbade his son not to waste his time.
options.B: The father advised his son not to waste his time.
options.C: The father ordered his son to not waste your time.
options.D: The father told to his son do not waste his time.

questions.explanation: Negative imperative sentences are converted into 'advised/warned [object] not to [infinitive]'. Note: using 'forbade' already carries negative meaning so it cannot be followed by 'not'.

questions.question: The mother said to her son, "May you succeed in life!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The mother wished that her son may succeed in life.
options.B: The mother prayed that her son might succeed in life.
options.C: The mother prayed her son would succeed in life.
options.D: The mother exclaims that her son might succeed in life.

questions.explanation: In optative sentences expressing a prayer or benediction, the reporting verb changes to 'prayed', connector 'that' is used, and 'may' shifts to 'might'.

questions.question: The boys said, "Hurrah! We have won the match." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
options.B: The boys exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
options.C: The boys said with joy that we have won the match.
options.D: The boys cheered that they won the match.

questions.explanation: Interjections of joy such as 'Hurrah!' change the reporting verb into 'exclaimed with joy that', and present perfect ('have won') shifts to past perfect ('had won').

questions.question: She said, "Alas! I have lost my purse." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She exclaimed with joy that she lost her purse.
options.B: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
options.C: She told with sorrow that she has lost her purse.
options.D: She cried that her purse had lost.

questions.explanation: Interjection 'Alas!' indicates grief, converting the reporting verb to 'exclaimed with sorrow', followed by tense backshift from present perfect to past perfect ('had lost').

questions.question: He said, "How beautiful the rainbow is!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He exclaimed that the rainbow was very beautiful.
options.B: He said that how beautiful was the rainbow.
options.C: He asked how beautiful the rainbow is.
options.D: He exclaimed with wonder that the rainbow is very beautiful.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences beginning with 'How/What' expressing admiration change into assertive clauses with intensifiers like 'very beautiful' and past tense 'was'.

questions.question: Ali said, "I can solve this puzzle easily." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: Ali said that he can solve that puzzle easily.
options.B: Ali said that he could solve that puzzle easily.
options.C: Ali said that he could solve this puzzle easily.
options.D: Ali told that he would solve that puzzle easily.

questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary 'can' shifts to 'could', and proximal demonstrative adjective 'this' shifts to distal 'that'.

questions.question: The commander said to the soldiers, "Halt!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The commander requested the soldiers to halt.
options.B: The commander commanded the soldiers to halt.
options.C: The commander told the soldiers for halting.
options.D: The commander asked the soldiers that they halt.

questions.explanation: Military and authoritative orders require reporting verbs like 'commanded' or 'ordered' followed by an infinitive ('to halt').

questions.question: She says, "I love reading novels." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She says that she loved reading novels.
options.B: She says that she loves reading novels.
options.C: She said that she loves reading novels.
options.D: She says that she had loved reading novels.

questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the present tense ('says') or future tense, the tense of the reported speech does NOT change ('loves reading novels').

questions.question: He will say, "I am ready." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He will say that he was ready.
options.B: He will say that he is ready.
options.C: He would say that he was ready.
options.D: He will tell that he had been ready.

questions.explanation: With a future reporting verb ('will say'), the tense in the reported clause remains unchanged in the present ('he is ready').

questions.question: The boy said, "Sir, I have submitted my assignment." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The boy respectfully said that he had submitted his assignment.
options.B: The boy said to sir that he has submitted his assignment.
options.C: The boy told sir that he submitted his assignment.
options.D: The boy said respectfully that he submitted his assignment.

questions.explanation: Honorific terms such as 'Sir' or 'Madam' in direct speech are replaced by the adverb 'respectfully' in indirect speech.

questions.question: She said, "Let us go for a walk." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She ordered that they should go for a walk.
options.B: She suggested that they should go for a walk.
options.C: She told to go for a walk.
options.D: She said that let them go for a walk.

questions.explanation: 'Let us' indicates a proposal or suggestion. The reporting verb changes to 'suggested/proposed that [subject] should [verb]'.

questions.question: The beggar said, "Please give me some food." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The beggar ordered to give him some food.
options.B: The beggar begged to give him some food.
options.C: The beggar asked me that give him some food.
options.D: The beggar told to please give him some food.

questions.explanation: Polite requests from mendicants or earnest entreaties use reporting verbs such as 'requested' or 'begged' with the infinitive 'to give'.

questions.question: He said to me, "What is your name?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He asked me what was my name.
options.B: He asked me what my name was.
options.C: He asked me what is your name.
options.D: He questioned me that what my name was.

questions.explanation: In indirect Wh-questions, the verb appears after the subject noun phrase ('what my name was'). Placing 'was' before 'my name' violates indirect assertive syntax.

questions.question: The teacher said, "Honesty is the best policy." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The teacher said that honesty was the best policy.
options.B: The teacher said that honesty is the best policy.
options.C: The teacher told that honesty has been the best policy.
options.D: The teacher advised honesty had been the best policy.

questions.explanation: Philosophical maxims, proverbs, and universal truths remain in the present simple tense in indirect speech.

questions.question: He said, "I bought a car two days ago." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said that he had bought a car two days before.
options.B: He said that he bought a car two days ago.
options.C: He said that he has bought a car two days before.
options.D: He said that he had bought a car two days ago.

questions.explanation: Past simple shifts to past perfect ('had bought') and the time expression 'ago' shifts to 'before'.

questions.question: She said to her brother, "Don't touch that wire!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She warned her brother not to touch that wire.
options.B: She told her brother don't touch that wire.
options.C: She said her brother to not touch that wire.
options.D: She ordered her brother that he don't touch that wire.

questions.explanation: Imperatives involving peril are reported with 'warned [object] not to [verb]'.

questions.question: They said, "We had already finished before he arrived." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: They said that they had already finished before he arrived.
options.B: They said that they have already finished before he had arrived.
options.C: They said that they had already finished before he had arrived.
options.D: They said that they already finished before he arrived.

questions.explanation: In complex past narrative sentences, past simple in temporal clauses shifts to past perfect ('had arrived') while existing past perfect remains past perfect.

questions.question: The stranger said to me, "Can you tell me the way to the post office?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The stranger asked me if I could tell him the way to the post office.
options.B: The stranger told me that can I tell him the way to the post office.
options.C: The stranger asked me whether can I tell him the way to the post office.
options.D: The stranger enquired me that could I tell him the way to the post office.

questions.explanation: A polite inquiry is reported as an interrogative clause with 'if', subject pronoun 'I', modal backshift 'could tell', and objective pronoun 'him'.

questions.question: My friend said, "Goodbye!" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: My friend bade me goodbye.
options.B: My friend told me goodbye.
options.C: My friend said me goodbye.
options.D: My friend wished me goodbye.

questions.explanation: Farewells in direct speech ('Goodbye', 'Farewell') use the reporting verb 'bade' (past tense of 'bid').

questions.question: He said to his friend, "Good morning! How are you?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He wished his friend good morning and asked how he was.
options.B: He told his friend good morning and asked how was he.
options.C: He greeted his friend good morning and asked how he is.
options.D: He said his friend good morning and enquired how was he.

questions.explanation: Salutations such as 'Good morning' use 'wished [object] good morning', joined by 'and asked' followed by assertive word order ('how he was').

questions.question: The judge said to the accused, "Call the next witness." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The judge ordered to call the next witness.
options.B: The judge requested to call the next witness.
options.C: The judge advised to call the next witness.
options.D: The judge said that call the next witness.

questions.explanation: Judicial instructions in a courtroom are commands, requiring 'ordered to call'.

questions.question: She said, "Must I attend the meeting tomorrow?" Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She asked if she had to attend the meeting the following day.
options.B: She asked that must she attend the meeting tomorrow.
options.C: She told if she must attend the meeting the next day.
options.D: She enquired whether she would attend the meeting tomorrow.

questions.explanation: When modal 'must' denotes present necessity/obligation, it backshifts to 'had to' in indirect reporting.

questions.question: He said, "Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He said that water boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.
options.B: He said that water had boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.
options.C: He said that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
options.D: He said water would boil at 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.explanation: Physical scientific laws retain the simple present tense regardless of the past tense of the reporting verb.

questions.question: She said, "I was cooking when the phone rang." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She said that she had been cooking when the phone rang.
options.B: She said that she was cooking when the phone had rung.
options.C: She said that she had been cooking when the phone had rung.
options.D: She said that she is cooking when the phone rang.

questions.explanation: In past continuous background actions with a time clause ('when the phone rang'), the continuous action shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been cooking') while the point action may remain in past simple.

questions.question: The coach said, "Bravo! You played exceptionally well." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: The coach applauded him saying that he had played exceptionally well.
options.B: The coach exclaimed with sorrow that he had played exceptionally well.
options.C: The coach shouted that he played exceptionally well.
options.D: The coach remarked that he had played exceptionally well.

questions.explanation: The exclamatory word 'Bravo!' is an applause/accolade, correctly transformed into 'applauded [him] saying that he had played exceptionally well'.

questions.question: He said, "Let me have a cup of tea." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: He requested that he might be allowed to have a cup of tea.
options.B: He suggested that he should have a cup of tea.
options.C: He ordered to have a cup of tea.
options.D: He said that let him have a cup of tea.

questions.explanation: When 'let' expresses a personal wish or permission (rather than a group proposal), it is reported with 'requested/expressed a wish that he might be allowed to [verb]'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly changes the demonstratives in indirect speech when reporting in a past context?

options.A: These -> Those, Here -> There, Now -> Then, Ago -> Before
options.B: These -> These, Here -> There, Now -> Now, Ago -> Ago
options.C: These -> Those, Here -> Here, Now -> Then, Ago -> After
options.D: These -> That, Here -> Where, Now -> Then, Ago -> Later

questions.explanation: Under standard grammatical rules of indirect narration: 'these' becomes 'those', 'here' becomes 'there', 'now' becomes 'then', and 'ago' becomes 'before'.
